purpose: Determine whether HADES direct Grocy recipe classification is a meaningful ordinary-chat latency target and record the routine-message logging defect found during tracing.

probe.implementation: AST-extracted exact function, helper and regex constants; logger replaced with no-op; no HADES module initialization or service connections
cases: Can you explain why Python generators are useful?
What's the difference between RAM and storage?
probe.latency_conclusion: The regex classifier is not a meaningful latency target in this sample; retain its domain routing until broader evidence justifies changing it. The timing excludes configured log-handler I/O.

privacy_finding_and_change.before: The classifier emitted the first 240 characters of every inspected owner/household message at INFO, including ordinary chat. The staged gateway log confirmed this on generator/RAM conversation turns.
privacy_finding_and_change.change: Removed the raw-message INFO log. No recipe classification, routing, Grocy access, or authority behavior changed.
privacy_finding_and_change.verification: Python compilation succeeded; source search confirms the raw-text log is gone. The existing Grocy Hermes runtime contract passed after making the pinned Hindsight provider available only under the temporary test HERMES_HOME. A new regression assertion routes a synthetic private sentinel through the classifier and proves no INFO log contains it.
privacy_finding_and_change.runtime_retest: Synthetic HADES Hermes runtime route coverage passed; no production runtime or service was changed. The isolated Hermes title/API harness remains inconclusive due profile startup constraints.

limitations: Synthetic ordinary messages only; not a full owner corpus.
No production or owner data was read.
No production deployment, hosted CI run, or owner dogfood was performed.
